subject.title: `before_agent_run` receives no input provenance; several producers never stamp it — internal wakes look like user input at the gate

question: Should `before_agent_run` expose host-authoritative `InputProvenance`, with explicit contractual classifications for every internal producer while retaining the gate's current fail-closed handler semantics?
rationale: Plugins may use this value for pre-model authorization and cost controls, so producer classification, absence semantics, and handler-failure behavior form a security boundary that should not be inferred by an automated repair.

options.title: Expose authoritative provenance
options.body: Add optional typed provenance, define every producer classification, preserve fail-closed hook errors, and require complete producer tests and live proof.

options.title: Expose advisory provenance only
options.body: Add the field but document it as incomplete or non-authoritative, which limits its usefulness for enforceable plugin policy.

options.title: Keep the content-only gate
options.body: Decline the API change and document that origin-based gating must occur outside `before_agent_run`.

recommendation.title: Expose authoritative provenance
recommendation.body: Add optional typed provenance, define every producer classification, preserve fail-closed hook errors, and require complete producer tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing provenance taxonomy and primary stamping pattern originate from their merged feature work.
